### Abstract

Provide a 3-5 sentence summary of your work on the primary task. Indicate what input data was used, what method was used for binary class predictions, what method was used for multiclass predictions, and what estimated accuracies were achieved.

> *Header and paragraph content was scraped from the raw webpages and processed into term frequencies of word tokens. For binary classification, a two-layer neural network yielded an estimated 81.4% accuracy; for multiclass classification, a support vector machine gave 78% accuracy.*

### Preprocessing

In one paragraph lay out your preprocessing pipeline. No need to provide exact step-by-step detail; just give an overview of the main components:

-   what text content was extracted from HTML

-   how text was cleaned

-   how cleaned text was represented quantitatively

Our preprocessing pipeline is built around extracting the main textual information from each webpage, including both paragraph text and header elements (both large and small i.e. h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6), to harness the detail within the main body content in addition to high-level summary descriptions found within titles and subtitles.

After, text was cleaned row-wise by sequentially removing urls, emails, punctuation, digits, symbols, whitespace, and finally, performing a lowercase standardization. 

Lastly, the text is tokenized, lemmatized, and the TF-IDF (Term Frequency - Inverse Document Frequency) matrix is calculated. This formulation quantitatively represents the cleaned text by describing both how frequently words appear with Term Frequency (TF) and how uncommon or informative words are across all documents (Inverse Docume Frequency). Collectively, this means that words will receive a high TF-IDF if they appear infrequently but contribute a lot of meaning, and a lower TF-IDF if they appear frequently but contribute little meaning.
